subject: chemistry-1
question: In a sealed hypothetical reaction vessel, 4 g of hydrogen gas reacts completely with 32 g of oxygen gas to form water as the only product. Which value states the mass of water produced, and which principle requires it?

options.text: 34 g, because a small amount of mass is converted to the heat released
32 g, because the heavier reactant determines the mass of the product
18 g, because one mole of water has a mass of 18 g
36 g, because mass is conserved in a chemical reaction

explanation:
The law of conservation of mass states that atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical change, so in a closed system the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants. Here 4 g of H2 (2 mol) and 32 g of O2 (1 mol) match the 2:1 ratio of 2 H2 + O2 to 2 H2O exactly, so both are fully consumed and all 36 g of matter appears as water. The energy released is real but the associated mass change is far too small to measure chemically, which is why chemical equations are balanced on an atom-for-atom basis.

ELI-10: A chemical reaction rearranges atoms; it never deletes them or invents new ones. Take apart a 36-piece structure and rebuild it into a different shape inside a sealed box, and the box still holds 36 pieces. So 4 g in plus 32 g in must come out as 36 g of water. Reactions release energy, but that does not make measurable matter disappear.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
